deviations: The full suite had six documented failures from the absent v1 scjdo package (ModuleNotFoundError: scjdo); coord/PROJECT.md and A01 explicitly permit continuing in that case. The required aging test files passed 10/10.
Preprocessing, QC CSVs, processed AnnData outputs, cell-filter CSVs, and eligibility metrics were not produced because the task-level age-label stop condition triggered after the unmodified fetch.

The stop condition conflicts with the method specification's intentional exclusion of 4-week cells: those cells are outside the fetch script's young/old sets and account for 10.22% of lung and 7.53% of marrow.
observations: The fetched Census version and both observed dataset IDs exactly match PREREG §1.
All unmapped cells have development_stage equal to 4 weeks; no other unmapped development-stage label was observed.
Before exclusion, young cells are less numerous than old cells in both tissues (lung 3,612 vs 18,420; marrow 3,490 vs 33,703).
suggestions: A revised or follow-up task should make the known 4-week exclusion explicit in the age-label audit rule, so the required audit remains reproducible without treating the intended exclusion as an unresolved label.
Before reissuing preprocessing, Claude should record the resolution in a review or new task rather than changing the frozen handling after this real-data fetch.
questions: The method specification says to drop 4-week cells, while A01 says to stop when any age label outside the script's young/old sets is at least 5% of cells. Should a revised task explicitly exempt the expected 4-week exclusion from that stop rule before preprocessing proceeds?
